sentences.text: Now the equipment that keeps a gasoline boat from exploding.
Any gasoline engine in an enclosed space needs ventilation to carry vapor away: natural vents, plus a powered blower.
Run that blower for at least four minutes before you start the engine.
Then use the best vapor detector aboard.
Open the hatch and sniff the bilge.
Gasoline inboards and sterndrives must also have an approved backfire flame arrestor on the air intake.
If the engine backfires, the arrestor stops the flame from reaching vapor in the compartment.
Keep it clean and firmly secured.
An oily, loose arrestor doesn’t do its job.
Diesels are far less explosive, but their spaces still need ventilation, to feed the engine combustion air.
